title: Wigner-Negative Magnon Steady States from Incoherent Qubit Pumping
abstract: We show that incoherently pumped qubits can realize a cascaded dissipative mechanism for stabilizing Wigner-negative magnon steady states. The mechanism combines qubit pumping with dispersive magnon-number selectivity to direct the steady-state population toward selected magnon Fock states. In the single-qubit case, the single-magnon population can approach unity, accompanied by strong antibunching and pronounced Wigner negativity. Extending the same principle to multiple qubits yields Wigner-negative steady states dominated by higher magnon Fock components. We further derive an analytical birth--death model that captures the mechanism and agrees with numerical results. These results establish incoherent qubit pumping as a controllable dissipative resource for generating nonclassical magnon states in hybrid quantum systems.
summary: The paper demonstrates that incoherently pumping multiple coupled qubits can stabilize Wigner-negative magnon steady states. This is achieved through a cascaded dissipative mechanism that selectively populates high-number Fock components of the magnon mode. It establishes this process as a controllable resource for generating nonclassical quantum light in hybrid superconducting circuits.
main_problem: The goal is to find an autonomous, number-selective method to generate Wigner-negative magnon steady states in hybrid quantum systems.
main_result: Incoherent qubit pumping successfully stabilizes these nonclassical magnon states by creating a cascaded dissipative mechanism that directs the population toward specific high-Fock components.
method: The analysis uses master equations, rate-equation modeling (birth-death approach), and Wigner function diagnostics to track state evolution under dissipation.
model_or_system: The system couples multiple superconducting qubits ($N_Q$) incoherently pumped to a single magnon mode ($\hat{a}$). The dynamics are governed by an effective Hamiltonian derived via Schrieffer-Wolff transformations, leading to number-dependent dispersive shifts and activated sideband couplings.
key_observables: Wigner negativity ($N_{	ext{neg}}$), magnon Fock state populations ($P_n$), antibunching signature ($g^{(2)}_m(0) < 1$).
important_parameters: The mechanism requires dispersive selectivity ($\chi$) and intermediate pumping rates ($\mathcal{P}/g$); pure dephasing ($\gamma_\phi, \kappa_\phi$) degrades the state.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on perturbative transformations (Schrieffer-Wolff) to derive effective Hamiltonians and uses rate equations as an idealized benchmark for population dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate single-magnon steady states showing antibunching/negativity, multi-qubit cascades mapping $P_n$ vs. $N_Q$, and parameter space plots correlating $N_{	ext{neg}}$ with target population stabilization.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the full master equation model to deriving an effective Hamiltonian via perturbative methods, then analyzing the steady-state populations using rate equations, and finally confirming nonclassicality through Wigner function diagnostics across varying loss/dephasing regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, controllable dissipative engineering scheme for generating highly nonclassical quantum states (Wigner negativity) in solid-state platforms by leveraging engineered coupling mechanisms between qubits and magnons.
